syllabus_topics: Object-Oriented Programming with Java and C++ Languages
Introduction to objects: definition; longevity; classes; methods; programs. Coding rules.
Operators, expressions and flow control in Java: precedences; assignment; operators; type conversions; literals; execution control.
Object construction: initiation and cleanup; constructors; overloaded methods; "this"; garbage collector.
Code organization: interface vs. implementation; libraries; member access.
Inheritance and composition: incremental development; "final"; class loading.
Enumerations; Exceptions; Collections; Input/output; Runtime type information.

Discussion and application of design patterns: Singleton, Null Object, Composite, State, Template Method, Strategy, Decorator, Factory Method, Abstract Factory, Command, Observer, Visitor, Adapter, Façade, Proxy.
assessment_rules: For the normal period, the final grade is calculated as 50% from the project and 50% from the exercises, with a minimum grade of 9.5 required for each component and for the final grade. There are specific deadlines for UML submission, intermediate project submission, final project submission, and a practical test for the project component. Thirteen laboratory exercises are to be completed in practical classes, with only the 10 best considered for the exercises component. For special periods, different scenarios exist based on whether the project or labs were approved in the normal period, with all normal period grades being discarded if neither component was approved.
